issues.title: feat(browser): load cookies from a startup file
issues.body:
Adds a shared `--cookies-file` startup option for MCP and CLI. It reads a
Puppeteer `CookieData[]` JSON file before the browser becomes available, including
HttpOnly and partitioned cookies, for both launched and attached browsers.

Imports affect the default browser context; newly created isolated contexts
remain empty. The file is read once per browser initialization and again on
reconnect/relaunch, without a watcher. Changing the configured path requires a
restart. Other cookies are retained, and imported cookies can persist in an
existing profile.

Invalid files fail initialization and trigger browser cleanup or disconnection.
Errors omit raw cookie data, and Puppeteer protocol diagnostics are suppressed
during import to avoid logging session values.

Refs #3470.

Validation: `npm run gen` (including lint/format) and `npm run test` passed:
2,002 passed, five skipped, no failures. Coverage includes shared configuration,
validation, cancellation, retry, cleanup, diagnostic suppression, and a real
Chrome check for HttpOnly cookies and isolated contexts.

issues.title: fix(browser): suggest custom profiles for missing port files
issues.body:
Fixes #889.

When channel-based auto-connect cannot find the default profile's DevToolsActivePort file, suggest `--user-data-dir` for a custom profile. Keep the existing running-browser/remote-debugging guidance and the original error cause.

Only add the hint for a missing-file (ENOENT) cause. Puppeteer uses the same outer message for malformed port files and refused connections, where changing the profile would be misleading. Permission failures also keep their existing behavior; those are covered separately by #3487. The README guidance for #889 was already updated in #3386.

Validation on Windows, Node 24.19.0, Chrome 157.0.8103.78:

- Updated missing-file regression fails before the fix; controls cover EPERM, EACCES, malformed files, and refused connections.
- `npm run test -- tests/browser.test.ts`: 41 passed.
- `npm run format`: passed.
- `npm run test`: 1,985 passed, 5 skipped, zero failures.

Updates `@google/genai` from 2.32.0 to 3.0.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​google/genai's releases.

v3.0.0

3.0.0 (2026-11-06)

⚠ BREAKING CHANGES

  • Default Gemini Developer API version is now v1 (was v1beta) (3f477bf)

    • Clients targeting the Gemini Developer API now default to API version v1 instead of v1beta.
    • No effect on Gemini Enterprise (Vertex AI) defaults: Clients with vertexai: true are unaffected by this default change and continue to default to v1beta1.
    • Some models are not available on v1, notably: the gemini-flash-latest, gemini-flash-lite-latest and gemini-pro-latest aliases, and some -preview models. They exist only on v1beta. To keep using them, use a specific stable model version, or switch back to v1beta as shown below.
    • Some model aliases are not available on v1, notably: gemini-flash-latest, gemini-flash-lite-latest and gemini-pro-latest. They exist only on v1beta. To keep using them, use a specific model version, or switch back to v1beta as shown below.
    • How to configure or restore the previous default via environment variable (Node.js): Set GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION (works for both Gemini Developer API and Enterprise / Vertex AI clients when no version is set in code): 
      # Restores the beta default ('v1beta' on Gemini Developer API, 'v1beta1' on Enterprise / Vertex AI)
export GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION=beta

      Or set an explicit API version string on either platform (e.g. 'v1', 'v1beta', 'v1beta1')
      

      export GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION=v1beta

    • How to set the API version in code: Pass apiVersion (or httpOptions.apiVersion) to GoogleGenAI (takes precedence over GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION): 
      import { GoogleGenAI } from '@google/genai';

      const ai = new GoogleGenAI({
      
apiVersion: 'v1beta',
      
});

  • Minimum supported Node.js version is now 22 (was 20) (7b9fbf0)

    • Following Node.js 20 reaching end-of-life (2026-04-30), package.json engines.node now requires >=22.0.0.
    • There are no runtime API or bundle changes resulting from this bump, and both CommonJS and ESM bundles continue to be published.
    • Users who must remain on Node.js 20 should pin to @google/genai@^2 (or ignore engine checks if supported by their environment).

  • interactions: CodeExecutionResultStep.result is now typed as Array<Content> | string (CodeExecutionResultStepResult) instead of string (b36ce99). The JSON and runtime value for text-only results are still a plain string, but TypeScript code reading step.result as a string may need to narrow the union (typeof step.result === 'string').

Features

  • Add source_text to AudioTranscriptionConfig and SmartTranscriptionMode. (ddb5158)
  • Add MALFORMED_RESPONSE to FinishReason (032d50c), refs #2937
  • cli: use gemini-3.5-transcribe as default model for transcribe command (df29944)
  • default Gemini API version to v1 instead of v1beta across SDKs (3f477bf)
  • Disable GenerateVideos for Gemini API, update tests/READMEs (3f65d02)
  • drop support for Node 20; Node.js >=22 is now required (7b9fbf0)
  • interactions: add Office and OpenDocument MIME types (b24cfc2)
  • interactions: support multimodal content in CodeExecutionResultStep.result (b36ce99)
  • support GOOGLE_GENAI_API_VERSION environment variable across SDKs (3f477bf)
  • update discovery doc (8be9344)

issues.title: fix(snapshot): keep extra element UIDs reusable
issues.body:
Fixes #3491.

Extra nodes returned by third-party developer tools share their retained element handle with UID lookups. Tools dispose that handle after use, so another action on the same UID or a later snapshot fails with `Attempted to use disposed CdpElementHandle`.

Return a fresh handle for each extra-node lookup, preserving the page-owned handle. This keeps these UIDs reusable across input actions, element screenshots, and script arguments.

Add a browser regression that clicks the same UID twice, disposes each action handle, and regenerates the snapshot. It checks that both clicks occurred and the UID remains valid. Before the fix, it fails on the second click with the reported error.

Validation on Windows, Node 24.19.0, Chrome 157.0.8103.78:

- `npm run build -- -j 2`
- `npm run format`
- `npm run test -- tests/TextSnapshot.test.ts`: 6 passed
- `npm run test`: 1,982 passed, 5 skipped, zero failures
